newsitem.title: UK: S&P says Poland trend fairly positive.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Poland trend fairly positive.

text.p: Standard & Poor's director Konrad Reuss said on Friday that Poland's credit trend was fairly positive and that the agency would be monitoring upcoming parliamentary elections closely.
"Currently we have a BBB minus with a stable outlook and certainly what we see in Poland is a continutaion of a farily positive trend," Reuss told Reuters.
"The political policy environment is always part of our analysis and in that case there are various scenarios of how the elections could unfold," Reuss said. "So we will monitor that closely."
Though no firm date for Poland's Parliamentary elections has been set yet, Reuss said it should occur by the end of October.
Reuss said S&P upgraded Poland's foreign currency debt two notches in April 1996 to BBB minus from BB.

"In June 1995, we assigned Poland a BB rating with positive outlook and than we upgraded them last year in April with a stable outlook," Reuss said. He noted that S&P also assigned Poland's local currency debt an A minus rating in April 1996 with a stable outlook.

Asked whether S&P's recent policy change to allow dollarized economies such as Argentina and Panama to have companies rated higher than the the sovereign ceiling would apply to Poland, Reuss replied: "For the time being, traditional policy of the sovereign ceiling stays in place for Poland."

"Over time, we will look at a number of countries that possibly can qualify for this dollarization criteria but in Polond one trend we can observe is a growing confidence in the zloty," the S&P director said.
He said assets in Poland were increasingly held in the local currency, reflecting strong confidence in monetary policy and overall economic management.
